mainTopic: Testing the מחלוקת of רב and שמואל about רבי שמעון's one-domain rule against two ברייתות, and whether a ברייתא supports רבי זירא in the name of רב about an alley without שיתוף.
overview: On the previous amud, רב and שמואל argued about רבי שמעון's rule that roofs, courtyards and enclosures count as one domain for objects that were there when שבת began. רב says this applies only when no one made an עירוב. שמואל says it applies even when each group made its own עירוב. The גמרא first brings a ברייתא about courtyard people and balcony people that seems to support רב. It answers that this ברייתא follows the רבנן, and proves it because the list leaves out קרפף and מבוי. Next comes a ברייתא about five courtyards open to an alley, where רבי שמעון says all six areas are one domain 'when they did not make an עירוב.' The גמרא defends שמואל in two ways. First, 'did not make an עירוב' really means they made no שיתוף for the alley. Second, רבי שמעון was only arguing on the רבנן's own terms. The גמרא then checks whether the line 'in the alley it is forbidden' supports רבי זירא in the name of רב. It rereads the line as 'into the alley' and explains why that clause is not redundant. The amud ends as רבינא begins a question to רב אשי, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא about courtyard residents and balcony residents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: when courtyard people and balcony people did not make an עירוב together, anything ten טפחים high goes to the balcony, and anything lower goes to the courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If the people of a courtyard and the people of a balcony forgot and did not make an עירוב together, anything ten טפחים high belongs to the balcony. Anything lower belongs to the courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to test the argument between רב and שמואל. This first line sets the scene, and the real proof comes a few lines later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The courtyard and the balcony above it are two separate groups with no shared עירוב, so each group gets its own areas. A mound or pillar ten טפחים high is easy to use from the balcony, so it is given to the balcony people. Anything lower is easy to use from the ground, so it is given to the courtyard people.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא is bringing a source as proof
Balcony or gallery. Upper-floor apartments open onto it, and stairs lead down to the courtyard
They made an עירוב, which joins domains so carrying between them is allowed
Ten handbreadths, the standard height that marks a separate area

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for the proof yet. These opening lines just set up the case. The inference that matters comes at the line 'אבל היו של רבים'.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
The residents of a courtyard and the residents of a balcony
who forgot and did not make an eiruv (together),
anything that is ten handbreadths high belongs to the balcony.
phrases.notes: For example, a mound or pillar in the courtyard.

phrases.english: Lower than this belongs to the courtyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a proof attempt on the רב/שמואל argument from earlier in the daf.
steps.raayaObject: Whether carrying between domains is forbidden when each group made its own עירוב (the argument between רב and שמואל).
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about the residents of a חצר and a מרפסת.

steps.title: When the separation rule applies
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא limits the separation rule. It applies when each group is many people and made its own עירוב, or when each side is a single person who needs no עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does this rule apply? When both groups were many people, and each group made an עירוב for itself. Or when each side was a single person, who does not need to make an עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now explains which situations its separation rule covers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each group is already joined within itself. That happens either through its own עירוב or because it is just one person who needs no עירוב. So each group is a complete domain, and the two domains stay separate from each other. The contrasting case in the next step is where the גמרא draws its inference.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case were these words said? This introduces a limitation
Many residents
Single residents, who need no עירוב
For themselves

phrases.english: In what case are these words said?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיוּ אֵלּוּ שֶׁל רַבִּים וְאֵלּוּ שֶׁל רַבִּים,
phrases.english: Where these (courtyard) belonged to many and those (balcony) belonged to many,
and these made an eiruv for themselves and those made an eiruv for themselves.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁל יְחִידִים שֶׁאֵין צְרִיכִין לְעָרֵב.
phrases.english: Or (where they belonged) to individuals, who do not need to make an eiruv.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא by limiting the rule from Step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The courtyard and the balcony are kept separate when each group made its own עירוב, or when each side is a single person.

steps.title: No עירוב at all: everything is one domain
steps.stepSummary: If the many residents made no עירוב at all, then the roof, courtyard, portico and balcony all count as one domain.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if they were many people, and they forgot and made no עירוב, then roof, courtyard, portico and balcony are all one domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the opposite case: nobody made any עירוב. In that case all the areas merge into one domain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here no one may carry from their house, so the house objects are already off-limits everywhere. Only objects that were in these open areas when שבת began may be moved, and they may move freely among all of the areas. This matches the idea that roofs and courtyards form a single domain.

keyTerms.meaning: Portico, a roofed area that is open on its sides
Roof
One single domain

phrases.english: But if they belonged to many,
and they forgot and did not make an eiruv,
roof, courtyard, portico and balcony
are all one domain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the contrasting case to Step 2, which completes the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When no one made an עירוב, the roof, courtyard, portico and balcony are one domain for the objects that were in them.

steps.title: Inference: with separate עירובין, carrying is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the ברייתא closely. They are one domain only because no one made an עירוב. That implies that if each group made its own עירוב, they are not one domain. This supports רב and challenges שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason is that they did not make an עירוב. That means if they did make one, they are not one domain!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from the ברייתא's wording and uses it as a challenge against שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא made 'they did not make an עירוב' the condition for being one domain. So if each group did make its own עירוב, carrying between the areas is forbidden. That is exactly רב's position: the חכמים forbade it in case someone carries house objects out. שמואל says carrying is permitted even with separate עירובין, so this seems to contradict him.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason is... This introduces a precise inference from the wording
But this implies...

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא never actually states 'if they made an עירוב it is forbidden.' The גמרא is reading that out of the condition 'they did not make an עירוב'.

phrases.english: The reason is that they did not make an eiruv;
but if they made an eiruv, no (they are not one domain)!

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּלֹא עֵירְבוּ, הָא עֵירְבוּ לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the key inference from the last clause of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's view that carrying is permitted even when each group made its own עירוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא makes being one domain depend on there being no עירוב. So separate עירובין mean carrying is forbidden, which goes against שמואל and agrees with רב.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows the רבנן, not רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this ברייתא is the view of the רבנן. The רב/שמואל argument is about רבי שמעון's view, so the ברייתא proves nothing against שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל by assigning the ברייתא to a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן also say that roofs and courtyards are one domain, and they agree there is a גזירה when each group made its own עירוב. שמואל was only explaining רבי שמעון, who is more lenient and does not make this גזירה. So a ברייתא following the רבנן does not contradict שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion is this?
The Sages, the majority view that disagrees with רבי שמעון

phrases.english: Whose (view) is this?
It is (that of) the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against שמואל from Step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the ברייתא to a different תנא (the רבנן rather than רבי שמעון).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the ברייתא reflected רבי שמעון's rule, which is what רב and שמואל argue about.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows the רבנן, who forbid carrying when each group made its own עירוב. שמואל's reading of רבי שמעון is left untouched.

steps.title: The wording confirms it: no enclosure or alleyway
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's wording supports the answer. It lists only roof, courtyard, portico and balcony, not קרפף and מבוי as רבי שמעון would. So it follows the רבנן. The גמרא concludes: learn from this.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is also precise, because it does not mention an enclosure and an alleyway. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer with proof from the ברייתא's own list. It then closes the topic with 'שמע מינה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's one-domain rule includes enclosures (קרפיפות), and he extends it to alleyways (מבואות). The רבנן limit it to roofs and courtyards. Since the ברייתא leaves out קרפף and מבוי, it must follow the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also precise. This means a proof from the exact language
An enclosure, an enclosed area outside the houses that is not used for living
Alleyway that courtyards open into
Learn from this: the point is confirmed

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא that seemed to support רב against שמואל follows the רבנן, because it lists only roofs and courtyards, not קרפף or מבוי. So it does not decide the רב/שמואל argument about רבי שמעון.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא method: a list in a source can reveal which תנא it follows. Here the missing items prove whose view it is.

phrases.english: (The wording) is also precise,
for it does not teach enclosure and alleyway.
Learn from this.

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּיְקָא נָמֵי דְּלָא קָתָנֵי קַרְפֵּף וּמָבוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in Step 5 with evidence from the ברייתא's wording.
steps.raayaObject: That the ברייתא follows the רבנן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא lists only גג, חצר, אכסדרה and מרפסת, and leaves out קרפף and מבוי.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא follows the רבנן, so the challenge against שמואל falls away.

steps.title: A new ברייתא: five courtyards open to an alley, and no עירוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא about five connected courtyards that open to an alley, where no one made an עירוב. The first opinion forbids carrying between courtyard and alley.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: There are five courtyards that open into each other and also open into an alley. Everyone forgot and did not make an עירוב. It is forbidden to carry from a courtyard into the alley, or from the alley into a courtyard. Objects that were in the courtyard when שבת began may be carried within the courtyard, but not in the alley.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new attempt to prove רב right and שמואל wrong. It starts by quoting the first half of a new ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion in this ברייתא, the רבנן, says the courtyard and the alley stay separate. So carrying between them is forbidden. Objects that were in the courtyard when שבת began may only move around inside the courtyard.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא is bringing a source to prove a point
An alley that several courtyards open into
Objects that were sitting in the courtyard when שבת began
To carry or move them

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Five courtyards that are open to each other
and are open to an alley,
and all of them forgot and did not make an eruv:
it is forbidden to carry in and to carry out,
from a courtyard to the alley, and from the alley to a courtyard.
And objects that were in the courtyard when Shabbat began:
it is permitted to carry them in the courtyard,
but in the alley it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first ברייתא was set aside as following the רבנן, the גמרא brings a new ברייתא that will include רבי שמעון's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the רבנן, when no עירוב was made, carrying between the courtyards and the alley is forbidden. Objects in a courtyard may only be moved inside that courtyard.

steps.title: רבי שמעון permits: all six areas are one domain
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון permits carrying. When the areas belong to many people and they forgot to make an עירוב, roof, courtyard, portico, balcony, enclosure and alley are all one domain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון permits it. רבי שמעון used to say: whenever these areas belong to many people, and they forgot and did not make an עירוב, then the roof, courtyard, portico, balcony, enclosure and alley are all one domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with רבי שמעון's lenient opinion. This is the line the גמרא will now examine closely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the first ברייתא, this one lists קרפף and מבוי. That is the mark of רבי שמעון's view, so this source really is about the argument between רב and שמואל. The key words to watch are 'they forgot and did not make an עירוב.'

keyTerms.meaning: A fenced-in enclosure, like a yard or storage area
A portico: a roofed area that is open on the sides
A balcony
One domain, so carrying between the areas is allowed

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon permits.
For Rabbi Shimon would say:
Whenever they belong to many people,
and they forgot and did not make an eruv,
roof, courtyard, portico and balcony,
and enclosure and alley:
they are all one domain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second, lenient opinion of the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון: when the areas belong to many people and no עירוב was made, all six areas count as one domain, and carrying between them is allowed.

steps.title: Inference: the leniency works only when no עירוב was made
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the words closely: the areas are one domain because no עירוב was made. That implies that if each courtyard did make an עירוב, they are not one domain. This supports רב and challenges שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason they are one domain is that they did not make an עירוב. That implies that if they did make an עירוב, they are not one domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the exact wording of רבי שמעון's statement to challenge שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל holds that רבי שמעון's leniency applies even when each courtyard made its own עירוב. But the ברייתא makes the leniency depend on 'they did not make an עירוב.' That sounds like רב's view: the leniency applies only when no עירוב was made at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason: the גמרא is pointing to the exact condition in the text
But this implies: introduces the opposite case that follows from the wording

phrases.english: The reason is that they did not make an eruv;
but if they did make an eruv, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּלֹא עֵירְבוּ, הָא עֵירְבוּ לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a precise inference from רבי שמעון's words in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's view that רבי שמעון's leniency applies even when each courtyard made its own עירוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reading the condition the other way: if the leniency depends on 'no עירוב,' then making an עירוב cancels it. That matches רב, not שמואל.

steps.title: Answer: the courtyards simply did not join with each other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that 'did not make an עירוב' means the courtyards did not join with each other. Each courtyard did make an עירוב with its own houses, and the areas are still one domain. That fits שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'they did not make an עירוב' mean? The courtyards did not make an עירוב with each other. But each courtyard did make an עירוב with its own houses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל by reading the phrase 'did not make an עירוב' more narrowly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of עירוב: one inside each courtyard, joining it with its houses, and one joining the courtyards together. The ברייתא only means the second kind was missing. So the case is exactly שמואל's case: each courtyard has its own עירוב, and רבי שמעון still says it is all one domain.

keyTerms.meaning: With each other
A courtyard together with its own houses

phrases.english: What does 'they did not make an eruv' mean?
The courtyards did not make an eruv with each other;
but each courtyard and its houses did make an eruv.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9 by redefining the phrase.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Did not make an עירוב' means no עירוב of any kind was made, which would support רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: It only means the courtyards did not join with each other. Each courtyard did make an עירוב with its houses, so the ברייתא fits שמואל.

steps.title: Pushback: the ברייתא plainly says they made no עירוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the ברייתא simply says 'they did not make an עירוב,' which sounds like no עירוב at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא says 'they did not make an עירוב'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer, saying it does not fit the plain words of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain phrase 'did not make an עירוב' sounds total, with no qualifier like 'with each other.' If each courtyard really had an עירוב, why would the ברייתא say they made none? This attacks the reading given in step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches: the text clearly says

phrases.english: But it teaches 'they did not make an eruv'!

steps.kashyaTarget: The narrow reading of 'did not make an עירוב' given in step 10.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plain wording means no עירוב at all. The narrow reading does not match what the text says.

steps.title: Final answer: 'did not make an עירוב' means they made no שיתוף
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that 'they did not make an עירוב' means 'they did not make a שיתוף' for the alley. Each courtyard's own עירוב was in place, so the ברייתא fits שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'they did not make an עירוב' mean? It means they did not make a שיתוף.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final answer: the missing item in the ברייתא is the שיתוף that joins the alley, not the עירוב inside each courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שיתוף מבואות is the joining that lets people carry in an alley shared by several courtyards. The ברייתא's phrase loosely refers to this missing שיתוף, while each courtyard did have its own עירוב. So רבי שמעון's leniency applies even when the courtyards have their own עירוב, just as שמואל says, and the challenge is answered.

keyTerms.meaning: They made a שיתוף: they joined together for the alley
The joining of the courtyards in an alley, which allows carrying in the alley

steps.whatToRemember: The second ברייתא follows רבי שמעון but does not disprove שמואל. 'They did not make an עירוב' means they made no שיתוף for the alley. Each courtyard did make an עירוב with its own houses, and all the areas are still one domain.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two joinings. An עירוב חצירות joins the houses inside one courtyard. A שיתוף joins the courtyards in the alley. The ברייתא says only the שיתוף was missing.

phrases.english: What does 'they did not make an eruv' mean?
They did not make a shituf (merging of the alley).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the pushback of step 11 by explaining what the phrase really refers to.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining a term (עירוב here means שיתוף)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The plain words mean there was no עירוב at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase means no שיתוף was made for the alley. Each courtyard's own עירוב was in place, so שמואל's view stands.

steps.title: רבי שמעון was arguing on the רבנן's terms
steps.stepSummary: A second answer to the challenge against שמואל. רבי שמעון himself holds that an עירוב makes no difference. He only mentioned 'they did not make an עירוב' to win the רבנן over on their own terms.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you prefer, say this: רבי שמעון was speaking to the רבנן according to their view. He meant: 'For me, it makes no difference whether they made an עירוב or not. But for you, at least agree with me that where they did not make an עירוב, it is all one domain.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer to the challenge against שמואל. It says the words 'they did not make an עירוב' were not רבי שמעון's own condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in Step 9 inferred from those words that if an עירוב was made, the areas are not one domain. That inference would help רב. This answer removes the inference: רבי שמעון holds it is one domain either way, and he only named the 'no עירוב' case as the easiest point for the רבנן to accept.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say: introduces a second, alternative answer
According to their words: arguing from the other side's own position
According to me (in my own view)
At least agree with me

steps.confusionAlert: This is not רבי שמעון changing his opinion. His own view stays the same: an עירוב makes no difference. He is only offering the רבנן a smaller point they might accept.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
Rabbi Shimon, according to the words of the Rabbis,
is speaking to them:
According to me, there is no difference if they made an eruv
and no difference if they did not make an eruv.
But according to you,
agree with me at least
that where they did not make an eruv
it is one domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לְדִבְרֵיהֶם דְּרַבָּנַן קָאֲמַר לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer, alongside Steps 10 and 12, to the challenge from the ברייתא's wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recasting the speaker's intent: the condition was a concession made in debate, not his own view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'They did not make an עירוב' is רבי שמעון's own condition, so an עירוב would change the outcome, which fits רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון holds it is one domain either way. The 'no עירוב' wording was only a debating point aimed at the רבנן, so שמואל is not challenged.

steps.title: The רבנן reply that the areas are two domains
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן reject even the smaller point regarding the קרפף and the מבוי. Even without an עירוב, those are a separate domain from the courtyards.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן said to him: No. They are two domains.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the next line of the ברייתא, read according to the answer in Step 13. The רבנן refuse רבי שמעון's offer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this reading, the רבנן reject רבי שמעון's offer. They agree that roof, courtyard, portico and balcony are one domain. They reject him only about the קרפף and the מבוי: even in the 'no עירוב' case, those are a separate domain from the courtyards, so one may not carry between them.

keyTerms.meaning: Two separate domains, so carrying between them is forbidden

phrases.english: And the Rabbis said to him:
No — they are two domains.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the reading begun in Step 13 with the רבנן's answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the רבנן, the קרפף and the מבוי are a separate domain from the courtyards, even when no עירוב was made.

steps.title: Does 'in the alley it is prohibited' support רב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the clause 'in the alley it is prohibited' supports רבי זירא in the name of רב. רב says that in an alley with no שיתוף, one may carry only four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: 'But in the alley it is prohibited.' Let us say this supports רבי זירא in the name of רב. רבי זירא said in the name of רב: in an alley where they did not make a שיתוף, one may carry only within four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to another clause of the ברייתא. It suggests this clause supports a ruling of רב about an alley with no שיתוף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'In the alley it is prohibited' sounds like carrying is forbidden even inside the alley itself. That matches רב's ruling that without a שיתוף, the alley allows only four אמות of carrying.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said: quotes an earlier line in order to discuss it
Let us say this supports him: offers a proof
They made a שיתוף (joined the courtyards into the alley)
Four cubits: the small space a person may carry within

phrases.english: The Master said: But in the alley it is prohibited.
Let us say this supports
Rabbi Zeira in the name of Rav,
for Rabbi Zeira said in the name of Rav:
An alley in which they did not make a shituf —
one may carry in it only within four cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רב and שמואל debate and examines a new clause of the same ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי זירא in the name of רב: in an alley with no שיתוף, one may carry only four אמות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's words 'וּבַמָּבוֹי אָסוּר', read as forbidding carrying inside the alley.

steps.title: Read it as 'into the alley' instead
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The clause means it is forbidden to carry from the courtyard into the alley, not inside the alley.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: 'But into the alley it is prohibited.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by rereading the clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban is on carrying from the courtyard into the alley. Carrying within the alley itself may still be allowed, so the ברייתא is no proof for רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (read it this way instead)
And into the alley

phrases.english: Say instead:
But into the alley it is prohibited.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof suggested in Step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof for רבי זירא in the name of רב, not רב's ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed 'in the alley,' but the clause can mean 'into the alley,' which says nothing about carrying inside the alley.

steps.title: That repeats the first clause
steps.stepSummary: If the clause only forbids carrying into the alley, it seems to repeat the ברייתא's opening clause, which already forbade carrying from a courtyard to the alley.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is the same as the first clause!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading from Step 16. It now seems to repeat what the ברייתא already said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's opening clause (Step 7) already said it is forbidden to carry from a courtyard into the alley or from the alley into a courtyard. 'Into the alley it is prohibited' would teach that same thing again, and a ברייתא should not say something twice for no reason.

keyTerms.meaning: That is the same as the first clause: a challenge that a line is redundant

phrases.english: That is the same as the first clause!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rereading offered in Step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading 'וּלְמָבוֹי אָסוּר' (into the alley it is prohibited).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that reading, the clause adds nothing to the ברייתא's opening ruling that one may not carry from a courtyard into the alley. So it seems redundant.

steps.title: The repetition teaches that the רבנן argue even without an עירוב
steps.stepSummary: The extra clause is needed. Without it, we might think the רבנן agree with רבי שמעון when no עירוב was made. It teaches that they disagree even then.
steps.simpleTranslation: The extra teaching was necessary. You might have said that the רבנן disagree with רבי שמעון only where they made an עירוב, but where they did not make an עירוב, they agree with him. So it teaches us that they disagree even then.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that the repeated clause teaches something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra line makes clear that the רבנן forbid carrying into the alley even in the 'no עירוב' case, the very case רבי שמעון asked them to concede. This keeps the reading 'into the alley' in place, so the ברייתא is still not a proof for רב.

keyTerms.meaning: An extra, seemingly repeated teaching
Lest you say: introduces the mistake the teaching prevents
These words apply only (limits a rule)
It teaches us otherwise

steps.whatToRemember: The clause means 'into the alley it is prohibited,' so it is no proof for רב. It is not redundant: it teaches that the רבנן disagree with רבי שמעון even when no עירוב was made.

phrases.english: The extra teaching was necessary for him,
lest you say:
when the Rabbis disagree
with Rabbi Shimon,
that applies only where they made an eruv,
but where they did not make an eruv
they agree with him;
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the redundancy challenge from Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The repetition is justified because it teaches something new
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן disagree only where an עירוב was made. Where no עירוב was made, they agree with רבי שמעון that it is one domain.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן disagree in both cases. Carrying into the alley is forbidden even without an עירוב.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The reading 'into the alley' stands. The ברייתא gives no support to רבי זירא in the name of רב.

steps.title: רבינא turns to רב אשי
steps.stepSummary: An introduction line. רבינא begins speaking to רב אשי, opening a new question that will appear in the next part of the text.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. רבינא is about to ask his teacher רב אשי a question, but the question itself has not appeared yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous section is finished: the extra clause in the ברייתא was explained (Step 18). This line opens a new exchange. Nothing is proven or challenged yet. Only the speaker and the listener are introduced. The real content of the question comes right after this line.

keyTerms.meaning: "He said to him". The standard way the גמרא introduces one person speaking directly to another, often to ask a question or raise a challenge.
רבינא, a late אמורא and a student and colleague of רב אשי.
רב אשי, a leading late אמורא, traditionally credited with organizing the Babylonian תלמוד.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for an argument or a ruling in this line. It is only an introduction, and the actual question starts on the next amud.

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
phrases.notes: Attribution and introduction formula. The content of what רבינא says follows on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the explanation in Step 18 resolved the question of the repeated clause, the גמרא moves to a new exchange between רבינא and רב אשי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Not yet stated on this amud. This line only introduces רבינא's question to רב אשי, which follows on the next amud.
